cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: A Valuable Safeguard
cards.instruction: Treat every delay, restriction, and extra step as evidence that the system is becoming safer and more thorough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've added a fourth inspection to our climbing wall. Leave the booking calendar closed; I welcome that extra safeguard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Opening is delayed another month. Shall I ask them to combine two inspections?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. A whole month without an uninspected climb is worth keeping separate. You can tell the customers I support the delay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll lose the season. They'll want their bookings refunded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Arrange the refunds under my name. Nobody will be tempted to use a booking before we're ready. Every cancelled climb is another risk the system has kept off our wall.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 denies B2 combined inspections because delay itself is protection; A5 directs B4 refunds as another risk-removing safeguard, making authority enact the endorsement.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 month/combined proposal causes A3 preserved interval; B4 season refunds causes A5 cancellation as protection from premature use.

relationship.evidence: B2 proposes efficiency and B4 reports customer consequences, a plausible operations colleague with material influence.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 refund burden as a further safety step, deepening restriction rather than adding unrelated good news.

specificity.evidence: A1 wall inspection and closed calendar, B4 existing bookings establish practical operations; closed calendar need not mean no prior bookings.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 each cancelled climb is a risk kept away follows the refund action; somewhat absolute but character-coherent.
